title: Union card problem keeps him from working with Chick
summary: As a Mobile union member with no New York card he was barred from working with Chick Webb, though free to work with others.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: about music. Of course, I didn't stay with him very long. I didn't stay with Chick very long. I'll tell you what happened. See, I had my Mobile card. I didn't have a New York 802 card.

Yeah. And I didn't belong to 802. So he talked to Chick and Chick got mad with him, and they got in an argument. So he said, 'Well, this man can't work with Chick.' I put in a transfer. He said, 'I'll tell you what I'm going to do, boy, for you.' He said, 'I'm going to let you put in your transfer. Now, I give you privilege to work with anybody else in New York but Chick Webb.'
Yeah. They got in a big argument.
But listen, Cootie, they never used to give you that privilege with anybody, did they? Didn't they make you sweat it out for six months?
No. Not back in those days.
No. So if I had of had my transfer in -- my card in --
-- it would have been different. But I didn't have no card in. I didn't think about nothing like that.

No. So he wouldn't let me work with Chick Webb. And Chick Webb said, 'Well, I ain't going to let him work with anybody else. I'll just keep him out here.' Like that. So Chick -- so he was taking care of me, and he'd give me a few bucks and --
Well, what was he hoping? He was hoping that the length of time would pass --
-- and then you'd have your card and you could.
He was hoping that. Instead, I told you about --
